title: Capital Asset Prices: A Theory of Market Equilibrium under Conditions of Risk
question: If everyone holds mean–variance portfolios, which risks get paid?
changed: The CAPM: only covariance with the market, beta, earns a premium; diversifiable risk earns nothing.
assumed: Common beliefs, one period, unlimited borrowing and lending at the riskless rate.

title: The Valuation of Risk Assets and the Selection of Risky Investments in Stock Portfolios and Capital Budgets
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
question: What does market equilibrium imply for the prices of risky assets?
changed: Derived the CAPM independently of Sharpe, from the investor's side.

title: Equilibrium in a Capital Asset Market
question: Is the CAPM a genuine general equilibrium?
changed: Stated the market equilibrium precisely and closed the gaps in the first derivations.

title: The Performance of Mutual Funds in the Period 1945–1964
question: Do mutual fund managers beat a risk-adjusted benchmark?
changed: Jensen's alpha: the intercept of a fund's excess return on the market's. On average, managers had none after costs.

title: Capital Market Equilibrium with Restricted Borrowing
question: What is left of the CAPM if investors can't borrow at the riskless rate?
changed: The zero-beta CAPM: a flatter security market line, anchored at the return of a zero-beta portfolio.

title: Risk, Return, and Equilibrium: Empirical Tests
question: Is average return linear in beta, with nothing else priced?
changed: Two-pass regressions: estimate betas, then run a cross-sectional regression each month and average the slopes.

title: An Intertemporal Capital Asset Pricing Model
question: What risks are priced when investment opportunities change over time?
changed: The ICAPM: assets that hedge shifts in future opportunities earn premiums beyond market beta.

title: The arbitrage theory of capital asset pricing
question: Can a pricing model rest on no-arbitrage instead of equilibrium?
changed: The APT: if returns follow a few factors, expected returns are approximately linear in factor loadings.

title: A critique of the asset pricing theory's tests Part I: On past and potential testability of the theory
question: Has the CAPM actually been tested?
changed: The CAPM only says the true market portfolio is efficient. That portfolio can't be observed, so tests with a proxy test the proxy.

title: Investment Performance of Common Stocks in Relation to Their Price-Earnings Ratios: A Test of the Efficient Market Hypothesis
question: Do low price-to-earnings stocks earn more than their risk implies?
changed: Low-P/E stocks beat high-P/E stocks after adjusting for beta: an early value anomaly.

title: Asset Prices in an Exchange Economy
question: How are asset prices set in an economy with a representative consumer?
changed: The consumption-based Euler equation: prices equal expected payoffs discounted by marginal utility.

title: An intertemporal asset pricing model with stochastic consumption and investment opportunities
question: Can Merton's many hedging factors be collapsed into one?
changed: The consumption CAPM: expected returns are linear in each asset's beta with aggregate consumption.

title: The relationship between return and market value of common stocks
question: Does firm size predict returns after controlling for beta?
changed: Small firms earned more than the CAPM predicts: the size effect.

title: The equity premium: A puzzle
question: Can a standard consumption model explain the 6% equity premium?
changed: Only with absurd risk aversion: the equity premium puzzle.

title: A Test of the Efficiency of a Given Portfolio
question: Are all alphas jointly zero against a given benchmark?
changed: The GRS F-test: an exact finite-sample test that the benchmark is mean–variance efficient.

title: Implications of Security Market Data for Models of Dynamic Economies
question: How volatile must the stochastic discount factor be to price observed returns?
changed: The Hansen–Jagannathan bound: the discount factor's volatility must exceed the highest attainable Sharpe ratio.

title: The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
question: Does beta explain average returns once size and book-to-market are included?
changed: No: size and book-to-market explain the cross-section, and beta adds nothing. 'Beta is dead.'

title: Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds
question: Which factor portfolios capture common variation and average returns?
changed: The three-factor model: market, SMB and HML, built from sorts, explain most of the size and value patterns.

title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
question: Do past winners keep winning?
changed: Buying 3–12-month winners and selling losers earned about 1% a month: cross-sectional momentum.

title: On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance
question: Is persistent fund performance skill or exposure?
changed: Added momentum as a fourth factor; persistence mostly disappears except among the worst funds.

title: By Force of Habit: A Consumption-Based Explanation of Aggregate Stock Market Behavior
question: Can consumption explain the equity premium and its predictable swings?
changed: Habit formation makes risk aversion soar in bad times, giving a high, time-varying premium.

title: Risks for the Long Run: A Potential Resolution of Asset Pricing Puzzles
question: Can a small persistent component in growth resolve the equity premium?
changed: Long-run risk: with recursive preferences, slow-moving growth and volatility news carry large prices.

title: The Capital Asset Pricing Model: Theory and Evidence
question: After forty years of tests, what is the CAPM good for?
changed: A survey verdict: the model's empirical failures invalidate most of its applications, whatever the reason.

title: The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns
question: Are stocks with high idiosyncratic volatility rewarded?
changed: The opposite: high idiosyncratic volatility stocks earn strikingly low returns.

title: Presidential Address: Discount Rates
question: What moves prices: cash-flow news or discount-rate news?
changed: Discount rates: nearly all price-ratio variation is time-varying expected returns, and the factor zoo needs taming.

title: Time series momentum
question: Does an asset's own past return predict its future return?
changed: Across 58 futures, a positive past-year return predicts a positive next month: trend following, documented.

title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
question: Are value and momentum special to US stocks?
changed: Both pay in eight markets and asset classes, they're negatively correlated with each other, and they share common factors across markets.

title: The other side of value: The gross profitability premium
question: Does profitability predict returns the way value does?
changed: Gross profits to assets predict returns as strongly as book-to-market, and hedge value.

title: Betting against beta
question: Why is the security market line too flat?
changed: Leverage-constrained investors bid up high-beta assets; long low-beta and short high-beta, levered to match, earns large alphas.

title: A five-factor asset pricing model
question: Do profitability and investment belong in the factor model?
changed: Adds RMW and CMA to the three factors; HML becomes redundant in their sample.

title: Digesting Anomalies: An Investment Approach
question: Can a model grounded in firms' investment decisions explain the anomalies?
changed: The q-factor model: market, size, investment and ROE capture most anomalies.

title: Momentum has its moments
question: Can momentum's crashes be predicted?
changed: Momentum's own volatility is predictable; scaling to constant risk nearly doubles its Sharpe ratio and removes the crashes.

title: Momentum crashes
question: When does momentum blow up?
changed: In panic rebounds after bear markets the loser leg rallies like a call option; a dynamic hedge avoids most of the damage.
